evidence: apps/api/src/__tests__/supabase-scoped-client.test.ts:13-57 and apps/api/src/__tests__/get-scoped-client.test.ts:30-92 — both suites assert getScopedClient allow-list selection semantics

findings.title: API defaults to the service-role DB client (RLS bypass)
evidence: apps/api/src/services/supabase.ts:198-226 — getScopedClient returns the service-role admin client unless the module key is listed in RLS_READS_ENABLED/RLS_WRITES_ENABLED and req.userJwt is present (platform admins always keep service-role)
apps/api/src/lib/rls-startup-check.ts:26-54 — production refuses to boot when the read allow-list is empty; an empty write allow-list logs an error only
apps/api/src/main.ts:12-14 — assertRlsStartupConfig(env) runs before app.listen
apps/api/src/__tests__/rls-startup-check.test.ts:47-64 — covers the fail-closed read path and the non-fatal write path
apps/api/src/services/supabase.ts:224 + apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:163-196 — every bypassing selection is counted (portal_rls_bypass_total) and every enforced selection (portal_rls_enforced_total)
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth still depends on middleware for the majority of call sites: 238 direct getSupabaseAdmin() call sites remain in non-test API code (vs 383 getScopedClient call sites) and the allow-list values live in GitHub secrets (not repo-verifiable). The startup guard prevents the empty-read regression in production only.
findings.recommendation: Keep the per-module rollout; additionally make the write allow-list non-empty a production boot requirement once the 17 write modules are confirmed, and add a per-module coverage assertion (see the partial-adoption finding) so the rollout can be audited from the repo.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: fail-closed production read gate + boundary metrics are present and tested; writes remain non-fatal and the secret-defined allow-list is not reproducible from the repo. Previous run: partially-fixed (ledger a97425d); status carries.

findings.title: No runtime detection or alerting for tenant-isolation (RLS) regressions
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:163-196 — portal_rls_bypass_total (module, kind, org_resolved) and portal_rls_enforced_total counters
apps/api/src/services/supabase.ts:221-224 — recordRlsBypass on every fallback, recordRlsEnforced on every scoped selection
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:94-112 — MCTTenantScopeRegression: >=50% of a module's RLS-bypassing traffic resolving no org for 15m

infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.test.yml:20-95 — promtool unit tests for both rules (fire / stay-quiet cases)

Residuals: the promtool tests are manual-only (no CI workflow references promtool — run via docker per the file header); the rules cover org-less bypass share and enforcement collapse, not RLS DB_ERROR/empty-result spikes; and a per-module E2E isolation assertion was never added.
findings.recommendation: Wire promtool check/test into CI (a pinned prom/prometheus image), add the DB_ERROR/empty-result regression signal, and add the multi-tenant isolation E2E assertion from the 20261002 test plan.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: metrics + Prometheus rules + promtool tests now exist (previously 'no RLS/tenant rule'); promtool is not wired into CI and delivery remains environment-dependent.

findings.title: Approved-membership RLS predicate reintroduced six times; pending/suspended members could access tenant data
evidence: scripts/check-rls-predicate.mjs:38 — BASELINE_VERSION 5302430; only newer migrations are enforced (historic files exempt)
scripts/check-rls-predicate.mjs:52-57 — matches alias/ANY/CTE spellings of the raw memberships predicate and exempts is_org_member / status='approved' statements
.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:53-59 — the guard runs in test.yml and validate.yml via the shared action

supabase/migrations/5302412_rls_approved_status_gap.sql:18-38 and 5302418_rls_approved_status_gap_2.sql:17-36 — dynamic rewrites of the reintroduced cab/hardware/client_portal/phishing policies to is_org_member
replication of check-rls-predicate.mjs (node unavailable): 6 migrations newer than 5302430 checked, 0 violations
findings.impact: New migrations cannot reintroduce the predicate; the historic set was rewritten. Residual: the baseline exemption is exactly why the live dv_update leftover (new finding below) survived — the guard checks new files, not effective state.
findings.recommendation: Keep the guard; extend it (or verify-rls.mjs) with an effective-state pass that replays drop/create across all migrations and fails on any live policy using the raw predicate.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: guard present and wired into CI; 0 violations in migrations newer than the baseline (Python replication). Cross-domain row (DATA area) — included here because the guard protects RLS policies; see also the new dv_update finding.

findings.title: RLS policies reference `manage` permissions that no role holds (dead predicates)
evidence: effective-policy scan (Python): live policies referencing catalog-absent permission pairs: contracts_insert_with_permission (contracts:create), contracts_update_with_permission (contracts:manage), contract_signers_manage_with_permission (contracts:manage), appointments_insert_with_permission (appointments:schedule), appointments_update_with_permission (appointments:manage), project_members_manage_with_permission (projects:manage), onboarding_update_same_org (onboarding:update) — all from 5302026
supabase/migrations/5302118_permission_matrix_full_catalog.sql:30-41,248-251 — the catalog defines tickets/projects/documents and onboarding as view/create/edit/delete only; no 'manage'/'upload' rows
supabase/migrations/5302131_governance_manage_permissions.sql:15-31 — 'manage' was added only for change-requests/dns-changes/risk-register

the 20261002 test plan (docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261002-0344-develop-6286137/37_supabase_rls_policy_deep_dive.md:470) proposed a lint 'every user_has_permission(org,module,action) pair in a policy exists in the catalog'; no such lint exists
findings.impact: Those write/update policies are effectively super-admin-only under a user-scoped client (admin/super_admin cannot hold a permission row that does not exist), so enabling those modules for RLS silently breaks non-super-admin writes and the DB disagrees with the API's permission vocabulary. Latent today because appointments/contracts/project_members writes run through the service-role client.
findings.recommendation: Either add the missing catalog rows (contracts/appointments/projects manage; documents upload/manage) and grant them to the intended roles, or rewrite the policies to the existing view/create/edit/delete vocabulary (as 5302129 already did for documents). Add the policy↔catalog lint.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: 7 live policies still reference permission pairs absent from the catalog (previously carried from the 20261002 run, never re-verified). Cross-domain row (ACM area) — subject is RLS policy predicates.

findings.title: document_versions UPDATE policy still uses the raw unfiltered membership predicate
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302081_fix_rls_policies.sql:25-30 — CREATE POLICY "dv_update" ON document_versions FOR UPDATE USING (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM documents d WHERE d.id = document_id AND d.organization_id IN (SELECT organization_id FROM memberships WHERE user_id = auth.uid())))
no later migration drops dv_update (grep 'dv_update' / 'document_versions_update' across supabase/migrations returns only 5302081)
supabase/migrations/5302112_fix_rls_approved_membership.sql — rewrote 24 tables but does not mention document_versions; 5302129 rewrote only document_versions SELECT/INSERT
scripts/check-rls-predicate.mjs:38 — 5302081 is below BASELINE_VERSION 5302430 and therefore exempt from the guard
findings.impact: A pending/suspended member of an org (any user with a memberships row regardless of status) can UPDATE document_versions rows for that org's documents via PostgREST with the anon key + their JWT — e.g. tamper with version_number/checksum/storage_path metadata — even though the API layer rejects pending members. This is the same class as DATA-P1-001, on one table, UPDATE-only.
findings.recommendation: New migration: drop/recreate dv_update using public.is_org_member(document org) plus the documents permission vocabulary (mirror document_versions_insert_with_permission in 5302129:600-613, e.g. can_read_document(document_id) for read paths and documents:edit for the update). Add an effective-state predicate scan so pre-baseline leftovers are caught.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: found by replaying all migrations (drop/create) and scanning the effective policy bodies for the raw memberships predicate; missed by 5302112's 24-table rewrite and exempt from the check-rls-predicate baseline.

findings.title: store_quotes public INSERT policy allows arbitrary organization_id after tenant scoping
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302105_store_quotes.sql:15-16 — CREATE POLICY "Anyone can insert quotes" FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (true) (no TO clause => PUBLIC)

supabase/migrations/5302132_store_rls_fix.sql:8-21 — drops the permissive 'Service role full access' policy and adds anon_insert_quotes/service_role_all_quotes, but leaves 'Anyone can insert quotes' live
supabase/migrations/5302408_store_tenant_scoping.sql:41-52 — adds store_quotes.organization_id and the member read policy (organization_id IS NOT NULL AND is_org_member(organization_id))
supabase/migrations/5302434_anon_privilege_least_privilege.sql:74 — grant insert on store_quotes to anon; 5302116 leaves the blanket authenticated DML grant in place, so authenticated can insert too
apps/api/src/routes/store/quotes.ts:68-84 — the API's public submission inserts without organization_id (NULL = public lead), confirming the intended contract
findings.impact: Any authenticated user (and anon) can insert store_quotes rows directly via PostgREST with an arbitrary organization_id. The row then satisfies store_quotes_member_read and appears in the target tenant's admin quote pipeline (spam/phishing/abuse, data pollution) without ever being a member of that org.
findings.recommendation: Replace the public insert policy with WITH CHECK (organization_id IS NULL) for anon/public (and keep service_role for org-scoped writes), or require is_org_member(organization_id) for org-tagged inserts. Add a behavioral test: authenticated user inserts with a foreign organization_id => denied.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: the tenant-scoping migration (5302408) added organization_id after the permissive public insert policy was created, and nothing constrains the column on direct inserts.

findings.title: Auth write endpoints call GoTrue admin APIs through the RLS-scoped client
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:305-308 — POST /sign-out uses getScopedClient(req,'auth','write') then supabase.auth.admin.signOut(token)
apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:380-381 — POST /reset-password uses getScopedClient(req,'auth','write') then supabase.auth.admin.updateUserById(...)
apps/api/src/services/supabase.ts:121-143 — the scoped client is created with SUPABASE_ANON_KEY plus the caller JWT; GoTrue admin endpoints require a service_role token
.github/workflows/e2e.yml:120 — e2e sets RLS_READS_ENABLED=auth only, so the write path is currently exercised as service-role
findings.impact: If 'auth' is ever added to RLS_WRITES_ENABLED (the documented per-module rollout), sign-out and password reset break with an auth error because the admin API rejects a non-service-role token. The module key conflates GoTrue admin operations with table writes that can legitimately be RLS-scoped.
findings.recommendation: Use getSupabaseAdmin() (or a dedicated admin client) for auth.admin.* calls; keep getScopedClient only for table reads/writes (e.g. the profiles self-read at auth.ts:75). Document that 'auth' write scoping is unsupported.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: scoped client + GoTrue admin API combination; latent while 'auth' is absent from RLS_WRITES_ENABLED (secret-defined, not repo-verifiable).

findings.title: No static lint for RLS role-gate drift or policy↔permission-catalog drift
evidence: scripts/verify-rls.mjs:6-19 — only three rules: tables must enable RLS; warn when RLS table has no policy; new migrations must pair create/drop policy
supabase/migrations/5302436_restore_platform_admin_rls_gates.sql:83-103 — the role-gate assertion covers exactly the five policies that migration touches, not future ones

the 20261002 report recommended lints (b) 'every r.key in (...) admin gate ⊇ PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEYS' and (d) 'every user_has_permission pair exists in the catalog' (docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261002-0344-develop-6286137/37_supabase_rls_policy_deep_dive.md:470); neither exists
this audit's effective-state scan found both classes of defect (dv_update, 7 dead-permission policies) with ~80 lines of Python — feasible as CI
findings.impact: The two remaining regression classes (short role gates after 5302436; policies referencing non-existent permissions) are only caught by manual review. The dv_update leftover shows the baseline-exempt static guard does not cover effective state.
findings.recommendation: Extend scripts/verify-rls.mjs (or add scripts/verify-rls-effective.mjs) with: (1) replay drop/create across migrations and scan effective policy bodies; (2) fail on the raw unfiltered memberships predicate in any live policy; (3) fail when a policy's r.key list is a strict subset of the platform-admin set unless explicitly allowlisted; (4) fail when a policy references a (module,action) pair absent from the permission catalog.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: consolidates the unimplemented lint recommendations from the 20261002 RLS report and the residuals of RLS-P2-001/RLS-P3-001/ACM-P3-005.

findings.title: Scoped-client adoption is partial: several tenant modules have no RLS call sites and service helpers bypass the scoped client
evidence: apps/api/src/services/satisfaction-pulse-widget.ts:1-505 — 17 getSupabaseAdmin() calls; the module has no getScopedClient call site anywhere (routes/satisfaction-pulse-widget.ts delegates to this service)
apps/api/src/services/dynamic-client-forms-builder.ts:1-74 — 10 getSupabaseAdmin() calls, no scoped call site

apps/api/src/services/approvals.ts:211-220 — addTimelineEvent writes module_timeline_events with the admin client and is imported by routes/approvals.ts, assets.ts, findings.ts, proposals.ts even though the routes themselves use getScopedClient

apps/api/src/routes/final/crud.ts:25-183 — generic CRUD for 10 tenant tables (sharepoint_plans, saas_audits, procurement_quotes, dns_change_requests, satisfaction_pulses, time_entries, budget_roadmaps, client_runbooks, custom_forms, backup_status) always uses getSupabaseAdmin()
apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:26-269, dashboard.ts:18, search.ts, bulk.ts:50 — admin-only tenant/aggregate reads
docs/RLS-rollout.md:19-23 claims the repo-level secrets enable ~44 read / ~17 write modules; the code defines 43 scoped module keys (grep), and the secret values are not in the repo
findings.impact: Adding a module to the allow-list does not guarantee RLS enforcement for that module: modules with no scoped call sites (satisfaction-pulse, dynamic-client-forms) cannot be enforced at all, and allow-listed modules still have admin-client helpers (approvals timeline writes). The rollout's true coverage cannot be audited from the repository, and the docs' '~44 modules' claim is not reproducible.
findings.recommendation: Publish a non-secret enabled-module manifest in docs/RLS-rollout.md (list of module keys actually set), convert the remaining tenant services/CRUD factories to getScopedClient (or document why they stay service-role), and add a static check that every module key in the allow-list has at least one scoped call site.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: 43 scoped module keys / 383 scoped call sites vs 238 direct admin call sites; services and generic CRUD paths for several tenant modules never consult the allow-list. Confidence medium because the secret-defined allow-list contents cannot be verified from the repo.

## Executive Summary

RLS is in unusually good shape for a repo of this size: **every one of the 137 live public tables enables RLS** (replicated scan matches the AGENTS.md/review.md count of 137/1021 exactly), policies overwhelmingly route through the approved-aware `is_org_member`/`user_has_permission` helpers (268/41 live-policy usages), all 18 SECURITY DEFINER functions pin `search_path`, the anon blanket DML grant was removed in `5302434`, the avatars bucket is declared with owner-scoped policies (`5302433`), and three CI guards (`verify-rls.mjs`, `check-rls-predicate.mjs`, `check-docs-counts.mjs`) plus a fail-closed production boot check (`rls-startup-check.ts`) protect the posture. Runtime telemetry for tenant-isolation regressions now exists (counters + two Prometheus rules with promtool unit tests).

The remaining risks are concentrated in three places:

1. **Effective-state leftovers** that the baseline-exempt static guards miss: `document_versions.dv_update` still uses the raw unfiltered membership predicate (pending/suspended members can UPDATE version rows via PostgREST), and seven live policies reference permissions that do not exist in the catalog (dead write predicates).
2. **The scoped-client rollout is partial and secret-defined**: 43 module keys / 383 scoped call sites vs 238 direct service-role call sites; several tenant modules (satisfaction-pulse, dynamic-client-forms, the final/ generic CRUD tables) never consult the allow-list, service helpers bypass it, and two `auth.admin.*` calls sit on the scoped client (breakage if `auth` is write-enabled). Whether "RLS is already enforced for most read paths" (docs) is true cannot be verified from the repository.
3. **One policy-level injection gap**: `store_quotes` keeps a public `INSERT WITH CHECK (true)` policy from before tenant scoping, so any authenticated/anon writer can insert rows tagged with an arbitrary `organization_id`.

Recommended next actions, in order: fix `dv_update` and `store_quotes` (new migrations), add the `webhook_dead_letters` DELETE policy, move the `auth.admin` calls off the scoped client, and extend `verify-rls.mjs` with an effective-state pass (raw predicate, role-gate drift, policy↔catalog drift).
